extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents, proprietors and patent attorneys filing or managing patent matters at IPOS (Singapore)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for filing, correcting, withdrawing, seeking security clearance, entering/cancelling Licences of Right, communications, and correction-of-error requests for Singapore patent applications before IPOS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for incorporation by reference (Section 26(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: To incorporate the description of an earlier application by reference the applicant must file: (a) a notice confirming that the description is incorporated in the application by reference to, and is completely contained in, the earlier application, as filed (Section 26(7)(a)); (b) The description (Section 26(7)(b)); (c) Patents Form 56 (Section 26(7)(c) & Rule 26(4)); and (d) A copy of the earlier application and its English translation, if any (Section 26(7)(c) & Rule 26(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that only the requirement for a copy and English translation of the earlier application is extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of incorporation does not replace filing drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement of incorporation by reference of the description does not replace the need to file drawings, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no drawings are filed on the date of filing of the application in suit, any drawings filed later may be treated as a part missing from the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: English translation requirement for earlier non-English application
rubrics_metrics.description: If the earlier relevant application is not in English, an English translation of that document is required to be filed with the Registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants need only provide the English translation of every part of that earlier relevant application in which the missing part of the Singapore patent application is contained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 26A(7) — Formalities officer review requirements for missing-part/incorporation requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the request is received, the Formalities officer will review that: (a) Application is a non-PCT national phase entry application lodged on or after 1 Apr 2007; (b) The application is not withdrawn or granted; (c) The priority application indicated on the form corresponds with Patents Form 1 or on record (if any); (d) A description is enclosed if the description or part of the description is missing; (e) Representation details and/or address for service on this form correspond with that on record (otherwise, Form CM1 or 2 is filed and approved); (f) The form is filed within timelines set out above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of the above requirements are not met, the Formalities officer will send a letter to invite the applicant to clarify or rectify within 2 months from the date of the letter. If not rectified, a reminder will be issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification options and form-selection guidance (corrections & updates)
rubrics_metrics.description: To rectify errors, the applicant may file Form CM4 and indicate the relevant rule (Rules 58 and/or 91). For updates to representation details/address for service (not correction of error), file Form CM1 or CM2 accordingly. To submit clarification letters or supporting documents, reply via eCommunications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using Form CM4 select appropriate correction type: 'Correction of Form lodged' for form errors; 'Correction of Specification of a Patent or of an Application for a Patent' for errors on the description; 'Correction of any other document relating to a Patent or an Application for a Patent' for other documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if objections not overcome for missing-part requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If the objections cannot be overcome or there is no response within the time period, the Formalities officer will refuse the request and notify the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary examination will not be performed on the missing part if the request is refused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval and examination if missing-part request satisfies requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request satisfies all requirements, the Formalities officer will approve the request and notify the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary examination will be performed on the missing part once the request is approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of missing part (Patents Form 56)
rubrics_metrics.description: After a missing part (Patents Form 56) is filed, it may be withdrawn as long as the prescribed period for doing so has not expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A missing part may be withdrawn only by giving a written notice via eCommunications within the prescribed time period. If the withdrawal request is in order the Formalities officer will approve; if not in order the officer will invite clarification within 2 months. If applicant fails to withdraw before the prescribed period expires, the missing parts will be treated as included and the date of filing will be changed to the date those missing parts were filed at the Registry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrar directions for information prejudicial to national defence or public safety (Section 33)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the information contained in a patent application is determined to be prejudicial to national defence or the safety of the public, the Registrar shall give directions prohibiting or restricting the publication of that information or its communication to any specified person(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person who fails to comply with the direction shall be guilty of an offence and liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $5,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years or to both.

rubrics_metrics.name: National security clearance initiation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: National security clearance process is initiated when a patent application is first filed in Singapore via Patents Form 1/8 or PCT RO101 (i.e., no declared priority date and is not a divisional application) and at least one of the applicant(s) or inventor(s) is a person resident in Singapore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National security clearance is not conducted for a patent application where Singapore is the office of second filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities officer keyword/issue screening for possible prejudicial content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Formalities officer will review the abstract/specification for terms which may be indicative that the patent application contains information which might be prejudicial to national defence or the safety of the public, e.g., projectile, unmanned plane, explosives, or firearm and any other information in the specification and abstract which might be prejudicial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the information is determined to be not prejudicial, a clearance notification will be sent to the applicant within 2 months from the filing of the patent application first filed in Singapore. Upon lapse of 2 months with no direction, applicant may proceed to file overseas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on filing patent applications abroad by Singapore residents (Section 34)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person resident in Singapore shall, without written authority (national security clearance) granted by the Registrar, file or cause to be filed outside Singapore an application for a patent for an invention unless (a) An application for a patent for the same invention has been filed at the Registry not less than 2 months before the application outside Singapore; and (b) No directions have been given to prohibit or restrict the publication of that information or its communication to any specified person(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person resident in Singapore who filed or caused to be filed a patent application without prior national security clearance shall be guilty of an offence and liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $5,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years or to both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'person resident in Singapore' for Section 34
rubrics_metrics.description: A person resident in Singapore could be an applicant or an inventor named in the patent application first filed outside Singapore, including a natural person, the Government, any company or association or body of persons corporate or unincorporated. It also includes a foreigner with a valid pass lawfully issued to the foreigner (e.g., a Singapore permanent resident and a work pass holder).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National security clearance is generally not required for a Singapore citizen who has been residing overseas for a period (e.g., at least 3 months) and who is not residing in Singapore at the time of filing the patent application overseas. The requirement is not applicable to persons residing outside Singapore.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Authority Sought under Section 34 — when required
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person resident in Singapore intends to file a patent application outside Singapore, without first filing in Singapore, he will be required to file 'Written Authority Sought under Section 34 of the Patents Act' to request national security clearance. This requirement applies so long as at least one applicant or one inventor is a resident in Singapore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Formalities officer will check the form for required information (see separate checklist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Checks performed by Formalities officer on Section 34 clearance requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Formalities officer will conduct a check on the information set out in the form, including: (a) At least one applicant or one inventor is a person resident in Singapore; (b) Title and abstract/specification are in English; (c) Country in which the protection is sought is indicated on the form; (d) Technology cluster is indicated on the form; (e) The request has not been filed and approved previously; (f) Keyword search for terms which may be indicative of prejudicial content (e.g., projectile, unmanned plane, explosives, firearm); (g) Any other information in the specification and/or abstract which might be prejudicial to national defence or safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of the above information is missing or incorrect, the Formalities officer will send a clarification letter and invite the applicant to clarify or rectify within 2 weeks from the date of the letter. If not rectified by the deadline, a reminder will be issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to Formalities officer on Section 34 requests — substantive amendment and name changes
rubrics_metrics.description: When responding: (a) To make substantive amendments to the abstract of the invention that changes scope, the request for national security clearance must be re-filed (applies to pending and approved clearances). (b) To change the name of an inventor/applicant listed in the request, inform the Formalities officer via eCommunications; if initial request pending approval the approval letter will reflect updated name; if initial request already approved a revised approval letter will not be issued but records updated. (c) If there is an inventor/applicant who is a Singapore resident at the point when a patent application is to be first filed outside Singapore and is not listed in the request, a new request must be filed. Removal of an inventor/applicant does not require informing IPOS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To submit clarification letters or supporting documents reply via eCommunications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing timelines and escalation for Section 34 clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no response from the applicant, the request will not be processed and the applicant will be notified. A clearance notification will be sent if information is not prejudicial; the Registry's response is within 5 working days from receipt for routine cases; urgent cases may be handled immediately if prior notice given. If potentially prejudicial, request forwarded to Government department/authority for advice (typically up to 2 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application is prejudicial, applicant will be notified and application will be put on hold after completion of preliminary examination and not forwarded to Patent Examiner or International Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minister for Law oversight of directions under Section 33
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister for Law will be informed of directions under Section 33 and will perform regular reviews to determine if the direction is still relevant; if no longer prejudicial, Minister informs Registrar who issues clearance notification and allows forward processing (search/examination or forwarding to International Bureau).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Registrar may extend time periods for doing certain Acts (e.g., request for search and/or examination) if they have expired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for alleged contravention of Section 34 and compositing offences
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is reasonably suspected that a contravention of Section 34 has occurred (resident did not seek clearance before filing overseas), the Formalities officer will identify whether offender is first-time and review reasons/mitigating factors to determine if offence may be compounded. If Registrar determines offence may be compounded, alleged offender informed to make payment within 2 months via IPOS Digital Hub payment platform (Internet Banking, Visa/Master card, debit cards, GIRO). Upon payment, the offence will be compounded and receipt issued. Non-payment or if offence cannot be compounded may lead to further proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person residing in Singapore may submit a Request for Composition with required information (details of overseas application, whether clearance was sought, mitigating factors, procedures to prevent future occurrence). Formalities officer will request clarifications within 2 months if information insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licences of Right (LOR) — purpose and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time after grant the proprietor may endorse his patent with a Licence of Right (LOR) to encourage licensing. Once the application to effect that licences under the patent are available (Patents Form 28) has been made, the proprietor will not be able to refuse to license the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The terms of the LOR can be negotiated between proprietor and licensee; if parties cannot agree either may request the Registrar to settle terms. Renewal fees payable after LOR entry will be halved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities officer checks for LOR entry applications (Rule 70(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt, the Formalities officer will review: (a) Fee has been paid; (b) Application has been granted and patent is in force; (c) Patent has not been endorsed with licence of right; (d) Representation details and/or address for service correspond with record (otherwise Form CM1 or CM2 required and approved); (e) If there are existing persons registered as having interest in the patent, they have been notified and there is no objection; (f) (duplicate item in source) If there are existing persons registered as having interest in the patent, they have been notified and there is no objection; (g) There are no other pending related requests (i-v: Reference to Registrar on Determination about Entitlement, Correction of Error (Form CM4), Application to Register/Amend/Terminate Licence (Form CM6), Application to Register/Amend/Terminate Security Interest (Form CM7), Application to Register Transfer of Ownership (Form CM8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any requirement not met the Formalities officer will invite clarification/rectification within 2 months. To rectify use Form CM4 with relevant rule(s) indicated; to update representation use CM1/CM2; to submit clarifications reply via eCommunications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval and publication of LOR entry
rubrics_metrics.description: If satisfied that the proprietor is not precluded by contract to grant licences, the Formalities officer will approve the application for entry and inform the proprietor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The event will be entered in the register and published in the Patents Journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of LOR entry — who may apply and core requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Cancellation of entry on LOR may be applied for by (a) The proprietor at any time after an entry has been made; or (b) Any person who claims the proprietor was precluded by contract to make the entry within 2 months from publication of the entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application made on Patents Form 28. Where entry is cancelled rights/liabilities revert to as if entry had not been made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and requirements for proprietor-initiated cancellation of LOR entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Where application to cancel is made by the proprietor, the entry on LOR may be cancelled if Registrar is satisfied there is no existing licence under the patent or that all licensees consent to the application, and the balance of all renewal fees which would have been payable if the entry had not been made have been paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proprietor liable to pay within prescribed period; patent ceases to have effect at expiration if payment not made (in some third-party scenarios).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party cancellation application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where application to cancel is made by a third party, the entry on LOR may be cancelled if the Registrar is satisfied that the proprietor was and is so precluded. The application shall be supported by a statement setting out fully the nature of the claimant’s interest and the facts relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Formalities officer will review against listed requirements (see Rule 73(1)/Section 54 subsections) and invite clarification within 2 months if deficiencies arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities officer checklist for cancellation requests (Rule 73(1) / Section 54)
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt, the Formalities officer will review: (a) Fee has been paid; (b) Application has been granted; (c) Patent has been endorsed with licence of right; (d) If request by proprietor, representation details/address correspond with record and there is no existing licence or all licensees consent; (e) If request by third party, the form is filed within the timeline mentioned and a statement setting out fully nature of claimant's interest and facts is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any requirement not met, invite clarification/rectify within 2 months. If objections cannot be overcome the Formalities officer will refuse and enter event in register. If satisfied, officer will advertise cancellation in Patents Journal for opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to cancellation — procedure and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may oppose the application to amend the specification (cancellation) by filing a notice of opposition via Patents Form 58 within 2 months from the date of the advertisement, accompanied by a statement setting out facts relied on and the relief sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPOS Hearings and Mediation Department will communicate outcome. If opposition successful the Formalities officer will refuse the application and update the Register. If unsuccessful the proprietor will be invited to pay the balance of renewal fees within 2 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of balance renewal fees after LOR cancellation process
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no opposition or opposition unsuccessful, the Formalities officer will invite the proprietor to pay fees equal to the balance of all renewal fees which would have been payable if the entry had not been made, within 2 months from notification (file Patents Form 15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon receipt of fees the Formalities officer may proceed to cancel the entry if satisfied there is no existing licence or all licensees consent. Where a request to cancel is made by a third party and proprietor did not pay balance fees within period, the patent shall cease to have effect at the expiration of that period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching for patents endorsed with Licence of Right
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person interested in obtaining a licence may look at the register for patents that are endorsed with a licence of right entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list of approved LOR is searchable via IPOS Digital Hub by using Advanced Search and selecting 'Licences of Rights' in the Search field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of application and form-level withdrawal procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant decides not to proceed with the patent application, he may withdraw the application by filing Form CM9. Any withdrawal of such an application may not be revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant intends to withdraw any Patents Form he has submitted, he may write via eCommunications; the Formalities officer will confirm withdrawal by notification letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund policy for duplicate submissions and search/exam fees
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant made or discovered a duplicate submission, he shall promptly withdraw the duplicated request and submit a Request for Refund to obtain a refund for the fees. For fees paid on the request for search and/or examination, a refund will be allowed if the Patent Examiner has not started work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other refund requests considered case-by-case. The Formalities officer will notify applicant of outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred channels and content for electronic correspondence with the Registry
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are highly encouraged to use the eCommunications module in IPOS Digital Hub to correspond with the Registry. Applicants’ intentions should be clearly indicated in their cover letter and the Application/case number together with Registry’s reference number should be quoted in full in replies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoting numbers assists routing to the patent officer(s) for appropriate action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct communication with Patent Examiner — permitted scope and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may request direct communication with Patent Examiners (IPOS International) to seek clarification on objections and comments in the Written Opinions. This does not replace nor affect procedures or timelines prescribed in Patents Rules for responding to the written opinion; they continue to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: (1) Send email to Patent Examiner (Secretariat) using prescribed format, including an email title like 'SG <app#> Request for clarification of the Written Opinion'. (2) Secretariat will discuss with Examiner and inform preferred time. (3) Applicant contacts Examiner at advised time. (4) Any response to the written opinion must be made in accordance with Patents Act and Rules and applicant must summarise their understanding of the discussion in their response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content/format when requesting clarification from Examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: The correspondence table to be completed when seeking clarification should include: SG Patent Application Number; date of the Written Opinion; name of the Patent Examiner mentioned in the WO; brief explanation why clarification is sought; full name of person seeking clarification; indicate whether the person is applicant on record or agent on record; e-mail address of person seeking clarification; date of this request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following the sample format helps Secretariat route and schedule clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of correction-of-error rules (Rules 58 and 91)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 58 relates to correction of an error in the register or in any document filed at the Registry in connection with registration. Rule 91 relates to correction of an error of translation or transcription or of a clerical error or mistake in: (a) A specification of a patent, (b) An application for a patent, or (c) Any document filed in connection with a patent or such an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court decisions (e.g., Novartis v Bristol-Myers Squibb) clarify scope — e.g., Patents Form 1 is treated as an application document (Rule 91 applies) rather than a registration document (Rule 58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for requesting correction of an error (selection of correction type)
rubrics_metrics.description: The source of the error should be corrected. If the error was made on Patents Form 1, select 'Correction of Form'. If the form has been approved and the error has been brought into the register, select both 'Correction of Form' and 'Correction of Register of Patents or Designs' as applicable. Details to provide: (a) Details to be corrected in the form and register; and (b) Relevant rule (Rules 58 and/or 91).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 23 Jul 2018 applicants may use Form CM4 and select correction types. From 18 May 2018 applicants should indicate relevant rule(s) (58 and/or 91) in all requests. From 26 May 2022 requests for correction of name/address/address for service must use Form CM4 instead of Form CM2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping of correction types to applicable Patents Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: As a guide the correction type and relevant Patents rule(s) are: Correction of Form Lodged — Rule 58 (documents filed at Registry in connection with registration) or Rule 91 (application documents); Correction of Register of Patents — Rule 58; Correction of Specification of a Patent or of an Application for a Patent — Rule 91; Correction of any other document relating to a Patent or of an Application for a Patent — Rule 91.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the table on Form CM4 to choose correct correction type. Forms relating to registration (e.g., CM6/CM7/CM8) and forms relating to application (Patents Form 1, 37, 11) are listed to help decide which rule applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting material required for correction requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the request relates to an error in any document other than a form, the request shall be accompanied by both the marked-up and clean copies of the proposed correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assists the Registry in assessing and implementing the correction requested.
